item.title: #3586417: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Audio-To-Audio Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +1768/−184 · php +1606/−180 · css +90 · js +58 · yml +9 · md +5/−4
  • Diff: 282ef3e
  • Discussion: #3586417 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Audio to Audio Explorer in AI API Explorer is rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. You pick a task (remove noise, restore phone audio, isolate voice) and only that task's options show. Results show the original next to the result in players, with the option to use a result as the source for another run. Runs that previously always failed with a "Configuration Error" now complete, and the generated code example is corrected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The plugin AudioToAudioGenerator drops AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() and uses the ai_provider_configuration element through providerElement('audio_to_audio', ...). File input is the shared ai_api_explorer_file element. Each run goes through executeRun(), so it is stored as an explorer run and results are rendered from stored runs by buildRunOutput(), with a per run code example from buildRunCode() using the shared CodeExample builder. New assets explorer.audio_to_audio (css/explorers/audio_to_audio.css, js/explorers/audio_to_audio.js) are registered in ai_api_explorer.libraries.yml; the JS only switches the run button label and hint per task.

The old failure came from passing the AudioFile[] returned by getNormalized() straight to saveData(). The new code treats every normalized item as its own file and saves each with runManager()->saveFile(), so a model that splits audio can return two files. The result file's extension and MIME type follow the audio the provider returns, with a notice when it differs from the requested format.

The audio to audio operation takes only the audio, so the task options (strength, keep room sound, sample rate, which part to keep, output format) are sent through the provider configuration. mapOptions() matches each option to a model configuration key from OPTION_KEYS (for example strength, noise_reduction, denoise_strength) only when that field can take the value (fieldTakes()). Matched fields are hidden from the model's own settings; options the model has no usable setting for are listed in a notice on the run, and the model uses its own value.

The docs page for the explorer is updated: the example uses audio/mpeg instead of audio/mp3 and reads getNormalized()[0], and the explorer path and name are corrected.

item.title: #3586409: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Moderation Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +613/−123 · php +572/−122 · css +34 · yml +6 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: 4b8a97f
  • Discussion: #3586409 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

The Moderation Explorer (part of the AI API Explorer module) has a new layout shared with the other redesigned explorers. Each check now shows a clear Flagged or Not flagged verdict with the highest-scoring category, and every category score as a bar, highest first, with flagged categories in red. The field is labelled "Text to check" and the button reads "Check text" instead of "Ask The AI". Each check is stored as a run, so results can be kept across reloads when run history is enabled. The generated code example is now correct: it previously used an undefined $input variable.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ModerationGenerator now builds on the shared shell from AiApiExplorerPluginBase (buildLayout(), runButton(), executeRun(), buildRunResults()), replacing the old getFormTemplate() and AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() flow with the ai_provider_configuration element via providerElement('moderation', ...). Submission creates a ModerationInput, calls moderation(), and stores flagged state, scores, flags, the provider message and token usage on the run. Results are rendered from stored runs (buildRunCard(), buildRunOutput()), and the code example is generated per run with the shared CodeExample builder in buildRunCode().

Providers return scores in different shapes, so findScores() handles both a flat category to score map (OpenAI style, with per-category flags read from the raw response's results[0].categories) and a nested categories array with probability or score and its own flagged. Only values between 0 and 1 count as scores. When no scores can be found, the raw information is shown as key/value details instead. Category names are made readable (for example harassment/threatening becomes "Harassment, threatening") and scores under 0.001 show as <0.001.

Styles live in a new css/explorers/moderation.css, registered as the explorer.moderation library in ai_api_explorer.libraries.yml. A new ModerationExplorerTest functional test uses the ai_test mock provider to cover the flagged and not-flagged cases, nested categories, and the code example. The docs page for the moderation operation now points to the correct explorer path /admin/config/ai/explorers/moderation_generator.

item.title: #3586410: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Object Detection Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +951/−206 · php +838/−206 · css +80 · js +24 · yml +9
  • Diff: 3abf58b
  • Discussion: #3586410 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

The Object Detection Explorer in the AI API Explorer module has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. Previously it showed detected objects only as numbers in a table and never displayed the image. Now the uploaded image is shown with a box for each detected object, labelled with its name and score, and there is a Boxes/Table switch. A minimum confidence slider sets which boxes start visible (lower-scoring ones stay in the response), and results are stored as runs with a code example generated per run.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ObjectDetectionGenerator drops its custom constructor and AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm() in favour of the base-class providerElement('object_detection', ...) (the ai_provider_configuration element), buildLayout(), and the ai_api_explorer_file element for the image. Submission goes through executeRun(), so output is saved on the run entity as width, height and objects; results render from stored runs via buildRunResults()/buildRunOutput(), and the code example is built with the shared CodeExample builder in buildRunCode().

Providers return boxes in different shapes, so pixelBox() accepts corner keys (xmin/ymin/xmax/ymax and variants), x/y/width/height keys, and plain four-value lists. Values that are all at most 1 are treated as fractions of the image, and results are clamped to the image. Boxes in an unknown format are not drawn but stay in the table, which shows named box keys as columns when all boxes share them. The image size is read with getimagesizefromstring() at run time to place the overlay.

A new explorer.object_detection library adds object_detection.css and object_detection.js (live value for the confidence range). The commit also adds an ai_api_explorer_test provider (TestObjectDetectionProvider) whose behaviour is driven by the file name, and a functional test ObjectDetectionExplorerTest using it.

item.title: #3586411: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Image Classification Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +1330/−215 · php +1084/−214 · js +133 · css +103 · yml +9 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: 25d2cf9
  • Discussion: #3586411 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

The Image Classification Explorer in AI API Explorer has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout. You can pick the image from recent results instead of re-uploading it, choose between your own labels (edited as chips) or the model's own label set, and see scores as bars ranked best first. A cut-off slider only hides low scores in the display; the full response is kept. Provider and model selection now use the ai_provider_configuration form element. Two bugs are fixed: scores no longer print as raw numbers (they show with two decimals), and the generated code example no longer hard-codes image/jpeg or pastes labels in unescaped.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ImageClassificationGenerator was rewritten on top of AiApiExplorerPluginBase: it builds the shared layout, stores each run through executeRun() and renders results from the stored run (buildRunOutput(), runBadge(), runMeta(), runActions()). The image field is the ai_api_explorer_file element. The provider is chosen with providerElement('image_classification', ...) instead of AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm(), and the old constructor dependencies (file system, file URL generator, provider helper) are gone.

Labels are parsed one per line, trimmed and de-duplicated case-insensitively. In "My labels" mode they are sent to the provider; in model mode none are sent, though typed labels are kept in the run input so editing a run restores them. Returned items are sorted by score, highest first, with unscored labels last. The result notes when the model used its own labels instead of yours, or which of your labels were not scored. Labels from the model are escaped before rendering. The cut-off is handled client side in the new js/explorers/image_classification.js (library explorer.image_classification): the server renders every bar and the script hides those below the cut-off, never the best one.

The code example is built per run with the shared CodeExample builder. The MIME type comes from the image data, falling back to the type stored with the run or a guess from the file name, and labels are emitted as escaped values. A new ai_api_explorer_test provider (TestImageClassificationProvider) returns fixed, unsorted scores for functional tests. ExplorerFile also casts the choice value to a string to avoid the PHP 8.5 deprecation of NULL array offsets. The docs page for the explorer has its menu path and URL corrected.

item.title: #3586414: Apply unified UX/design and Provider Config element to Text-To-Speech Generation Explorer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +2102/−210 · php +1650/−209 · js +234 · css +204 · yml +13 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: dbbf52a
  • Discussion: #3586414 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

The Text to Speech explorer in the AI API Explorer module has been rebuilt on the shared explorer layout and now uses the AI provider configuration element for provider and model selection. Voices appear as a grid with a play button for a short sample of each. A "Compare voices" switch lets one run generate up to three versions side by side, each with its own player and code example. Voices the selected model rejects are disabled, and the format hint says PCM cannot play in a browser. Audio is now saved and played in the format you picked instead of always as MP3, and the generated code example no longer calls a non-existent method.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

TextToSpeechGenerator (plugin ID text_to_speech_generator, so the explorer path is now /admin/config/ai/explorers/text_to_speech_generator) builds its form with the ai_provider_configuration element in place of AiProviderFormHelper::generateAiProvidersForm(). Voice and format are no longer repeated in the provider config; they come from the model's configuration schema through processVoices() and processFormat(). Rejected voices are disabled in the form, and validateVoices() refuses a submission whose voice the submitted model rejects, or more than three voices when comparing.

Each run is stored through the shared run history, with a version per voice. A voice that fails does not fail the run unless every voice fails, and failed runs are kept with the error and a Retry button. Files get the extension and MIME type of the chosen format (for example speech-nova.opus as audio/ogg), also when saved as media. The per-run code example now uses $output->getRawOutput() instead of getRaw(). PCM versions get a download link instead of a playable preview.

Voice samples are made on demand by the static ajaxSample() callback, which returns an aieTtsSample AJAX command. A sample is generated once per model and voice and the file is reused, and is regenerated if its file is gone. The new library explorer.text_to_speech in ai_api_explorer.libraries.yml adds css/explorers/text_to_speech.css and js/explorers/text_to_speech.js. A test provider (ai_api_explorer_test_text_to_speech) and functional and kernel tests were added. The developer docs were updated for the new path. I could not read the plugin diff itself, only the surrounding diff, and checked the method names against the repo.

item.title: #3601419: Trust DDEV’s local CA in snap Firefox and Chromium on Linux
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +116/−13 · bats +71/−2 · sh +43/−10 · txt +1 · md +1/−1
  • Diff: ad3fd9d
  • Discussion: #3601419 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

On Linux desktops where Firefox or Chromium is installed as a snap (the Ubuntu default), the installer now adds DDEV's local certificate authority directly to the browser's own certificate store. Previously mkcert -install could not reach that store, so https://<project>.ddev.site still showed a security warning. After the installer runs, restart the browser if it is open. A snap browser that has never been opened has no certificate store yet, so the installer still prints the manual import steps for it.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

_warn_snap_browsers in src/lib/platform/ensure_local_https.sh is replaced by _trust_snap_browsers, called from ensure_local_https on Linux after mkcert -install. For each of ~/snap/firefox and ~/snap/chromium that exists, it collects NSS database directories: every ~/snap/firefox/common/.mozilla/firefox/*/ containing cert9.db, and ~/snap/chromium/current/.pki/nssdb if it has cert9.db. The new helper _add_ca_to_nss_dbs runs certutil -A -d "sql:<dir>" -t "C,," -n "mkcert development CA (DDEV)" -i "$(mkcert -CAROOT)/rootCA.pem" on each one, and fails if certutil is missing or any add fails.

The issue proposed skipping databases that already hold the CA, but the code does not check first. A comment in the code says re-adding the same CA is harmless. Browsers that were updated print an ok message asking for a restart. Browsers with no database, or where certutil fails, print the existing warning with manual import instructions. The function always returns 0, so the step stays best-effort. New bats tests cover multiple Firefox profiles, the Chromium nssdb, no-profile, missing certutil, a failing certutil -A, and macOS. AGENTS.md and the spelling dictionary (nssdb) are updated.

Contribution

item.title: #3601418: --yolo still prompts for a project name when a config source is given
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +144/−16 · bats +114/−6 · sh +23/−8 · md +7/−2
  • Diff: 50be52e
  • Discussion: #3601418 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

In the One Line Installer, --yolo now takes the default project directory without asking even when a config source is given (--config-url, --config-path, --global-config, or a positional source). Before, those runs stopped at "Enter a name for the new project" and failed with /dev/tty: Device not configured when no terminal was available. The GitHub repository questions are skipped in the same case. The interactive "Use a config" menu still asks for a name.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

step_create_project_dir only took the default silently when YOLO=1 and USE_CONFIG=0, and every config loader sets USE_CONFIG=1. The "Use a config" menu sets YOLO=1 itself, so YOLO alone can't tell the user's own flag from the menu. The fix adds YOLO_FLAG, set in setup_site_command.sh right after YOLO is read from args[--yolo], and a new helper yolo_takes_defaults (src/lib/core/yolo_takes_defaults.sh). It returns true when YOLO_FLAG=1, or when YOLO=1 with USE_CONFIG=0.

step_create_project_dir (the in-place empty directory default, the free default name, and the existing-directory warning path) and github_setup now call this helper instead of testing YOLO/USE_CONFIG directly. An existing default directory still produces a warning and, with no terminal, dies with the --name guidance. Bats tests cover the helper, YOLO_FLAG, and the create-dir and GitHub steps, and AGENTS.md documents the new global.

item.title: #3601417: DDEV's usage-statistics prompt blocks unattended (--yolo) installs
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +38/−3 · bats +25 · sh +6 · md +5/−2 · 1 +1 · yml +1/−1
  • Diff: d74be52
  • Discussion: #3601417 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

Unattended installs run with --yolo no longer stop at "Starting DDEV..." waiting for an answer to DDEV's "May we send anonymous DDEV usage statistics?" question. That question appears on the first ddev start after DDEV is installed or upgraded, so it always appeared on a fresh machine. Under --yolo the prompt is now skipped and no usage data is sent. Interactive runs are unchanged.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

setup_site_command.sh (and its generated copy) now exports DDEV_NO_INSTRUMENTATION=true right after ASK_UNATTENDED is set from YOLO, before run_install runs any DDEV command. The condition is ASK_UNATTENDED -eq 1, so any unattended run triggers it, including config-driven runs, not only --yolo. The export uses ${DDEV_NO_INSTRUMENTATION:-true}, so a value the user already set (for example false) is kept. DDEV's global configuration is not modified.

The --yolo help text was updated in the CLI spec, usage output, man page and docs, and bats tests cover the three cases: exported under --yolo, unset for interactive runs, and a user-set value preserved.

item.title: #3601416: Add certutil on Linux
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +199/−3 · bats +137 · sh +57/−1 · md +4/−2 · txt +1
  • Diff: 4cd205c
  • Discussion: #3601416 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

On a fresh Linux machine the installer now sets up browser trust for DDEV's local certificate authority, so https://<project>.ddev.site no longer shows a certificate warning that has to be accepted by hand. It installs the missing NSS tools and runs mkcert -install even when DDEV was already installed. For snap-packaged Firefox or Chromium, which keep their own certificate store, it prints instructions for importing the CA manually.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Adds ensure_local_https in src/lib/platform/ensure_local_https.sh, called from step_ensure_ddev after _ensure_ddev_cli and before ensure_git, as ensure_local_https || true, so failure never aborts the install. DDEV's install.sh only runs mkcert -install when it installs DDEV itself, and on Linux mkcert can only write to Chrome/Firefox NSS stores through certutil, which nothing installed.

The function warns and returns 1 if mkcert is missing. On Linux it calls _ensure_certutil, which installs libnss3-tools via apt or nss-tools via dnf depending on PKG, and warns if PKG is empty (unmapped distro) or the install fails. It then runs mkcert -install. On Linux, _warn_snap_browsers checks for ~/snap/firefox and ~/snap/chromium and, if found, warns to import $(mkcert -CAROOT)/rootCA.pem through the browser's certificate settings. macOS gets no package install. New bats tests cover each branch, and the step_ensure_ddev tests cover the call order and the carry-on-on-failure behaviour.

item.title: #3586778: Shared AI API Explorer input picker: recent results, media library or upload
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +2428/−0 · php +1836 · css +309 · js +263 · yml +20
  • Diff: 1291c9d
  • Discussion: #3586778 · 1 contributor · 22 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer module gets a shared input picker for explorers that take an image or audio file. The user can choose a recent result from their own explorer runs, pick an item from the media library, or upload a file. A preview shows the chosen file with its type, size, and dimensions or length. Without run history the recent results are not shown. If Media or Media Library is off, the media option is replaced by a note giving the reason, or by a plain media autocomplete when only Media Library is missing. The commit shows the element working in a test explorer. The diff I could read does not show the existing file-input explorers being switched to it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_file form element (Drupal\ai_api_explorer\Element\ExplorerFile) with ExplorerFile::toOperationFile(), plus a media_library.opener service and an ai_api_explorer.file_forget route.

Technical details

The picker is a new form element, ExplorerFile (#type ai_api_explorer_file), in modules/ai_api_explorer/src/Element/ExplorerFile.php. Its value is ['fid' => ..., 'source' => 'recent'|'media'|'upload']. Properties are #media_type (image, audio or video), #operation_type, #extensions, #recent and #media. Accepted extensions come from #extensions, else from the OPERATION_EXTENSIONS map for the operation type (for example speech_to_text audio: mp3 m4a mp4 wav webm ogg flac), else from per-media-type defaults. Every source goes through ExplorerFile::accepts(), which checks extension and MIME type. A recent result or media item therefore cannot bring in a format that an upload would be refused for. MP4 and WebM files that Drupal detects as video are allowed as audio.

On validation, a recent or uploaded file must belong to the current user and the user needs access ai prompt. Uploads must also be files stored by the explorers (isRunFile()). Media items must pass access('view') and belong to a media type whose source is the right kind. ExplorerFile::toOperationFile() turns the file entity into an ImageFile, AudioFile, VideoFile or GenericFile carrying the file's real MIME type.

When Media Library is enabled, a new AiApiExplorerServiceProvider registers ExplorerFileOpener as a media_library.opener. It returns the picked item to the picker by AJAX and refuses files the picker does not accept. A required picker with no default value takes the ?file= query parameter, which is how "Use as source" links can preselect a file. This only works for the user's own files stored by the explorers. A new ai_api_explorer.file_forget POST route and a hover button on the thumbnails let users remove a file from recent files. A file library (explorer-file.js and explorer-file.css) drives the preview and the clear and remove buttons. The commit also adds a PickerTestExplorer in ai_api_explorer_test, which calls useAsSourceLink() from the plugin base class. Kernel and functional tests were added but were not in the diff I could read.

Upgrade

Explorer plugin authors can replace a custom upload field with the element:

$form['setup']['image'] = [
  '#type' => 'ai_api_explorer_file',
  '#title' => $this->t('Source image'),
  '#media_type' => 'image',
  '#extensions' => 'png jpg jpeg',
  '#required' => TRUE,
];

Then on submit, turn the picked file into an operation input:

$value = $form_state->getValue('image');
$operation_file = ExplorerFile::toOperationFile(File::load($value['fid']));

item.title: #3586775: Redesign the AI API Explorers list as a hub that survives a broken provider
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +1128/−214 · php +661/−211 · css +319/−1 · twig +89 · js +49 · yml +10/−2
  • Diff: 0750658
  • Discussion: #3586775 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorers page at /admin/config/ai/explorers is now a hub of cards grouped by type (Text, Search and ranking, Image, Audio and video, Tools and more). Each card shows the explorer name, description and the providers that can serve it. Explorers with no usable provider stay in the list, dimmed, with a "No provider yet · Set up" label instead of disappearing. There is a search box, type filters and an "Only ready to use" checkbox. A provider that throws while the page checks which providers are usable no longer takes the page down: a notice and a per-card warning appear and the error is logged. An explorer that fails to load is shown as a broken card and logged, and a router rebuild no longer fails because of it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The explorers list is rendered by the new ai-api-explorer-hub.html.twig template instead of the core admin block list.
  • API change: ExplorerSetupList controller removed in favor of ExplorerHub; AiApiExplorerAccessChecker constructor now takes a logger.
  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_hub theme hook and ai_api_explorer/hub library; new ExplorerHub controller on the existing ai_api_explorer.list_page route.

Technical details

The route ai_api_explorer.list_page now points to the new ExplorerHub::build() controller, which replaces ExplorerSetupList and its SystemManager::getBlockContents() output. It renders the new ai_api_explorer_hub theme hook (template ai-api-explorer-hub.html.twig, preprocess template_preprocess_ai_api_explorer_hub) and attaches the new ai_api_explorer/hub library (explorer-hub.css, explorer-hub.js). The search, type filter and ready filter work client side on data-* attributes. Explorers are assigned to groups by their operation types, using the ExplorerHub::GROUPS constant, with other as the fallback. Provider usability comes from the ai_api_explorer.availability service (getProviders(), getFailures()), and cards use getHubSummary() when an explorer plugin provides one. Each explorer is built inside a try/catch (\Throwable). A failure is logged to the ai_api_explorer logger channel and shown as a broken card with no link.

Hardening elsewhere: AiApiExplorerRouteSubscriber::alterRoutes() no longer instantiates every explorer. It takes the route title from the plugin definition, so a plugin that throws in create() cannot break a router rebuild. AiApiExplorerAccessChecker now takes the logger as a second constructor argument. Summary

The AI API Explorer now has shared viewers for file results. An audio player draws a waveform and has play/pause, click-to-seek, a speed button, duration and download. Formats browsers cannot play, such as raw PCM, show a note and a download link instead. Images open full size in a dialog with their details and a download link, and transparent images sit on a checkerboard. There is also a before/after image comparison with a slider or side-by-side mode, and a box overlay with a minimum-confidence slider and label toggles. A style guide explorer in the test module shows each viewer with sample files. Explorers such as text to speech, text to image and object detection can use these viewers without writing their own markup.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Six new Twig templates (ai-api-explorer-*.html.twig) that themes can override.
  • New API: New theme hooks ai_api_explorer_audio, ai_api_explorer_image, ai_api_explorer_compare, ai_api_explorer_boxes, ai_api_explorer_audio_compare and ai_api_explorer_bars, with templates and an ai_api_explorer/media library.

Technical details

The commit registers the theme hooks in Hook\AiApiExplorer, each with an initial preprocess function in ai_api_explorer.module. Each has a Twig template, and the audio and image templates take their icons from ExplorerUi::icon(). The matching ExplorerUi builder methods (audio(), image(), audioCompare(), compare(), boxes(), bars()) already existed in the module. Each one attaches the new ai_api_explorer/media library, which depends on explorer_ui and adds css/explorer-media.css and js/explorer-media.js.

The preprocess functions do the computation. For boxes, pixel coordinates become percentages of the image size, and the box labels are counted for the toggle buttons. For bars, values are clamped between 0 and 1 and given CSS classes. Image and compare templates get an aspect-ratio from width and height when both are known.

The behaviors in explorer-media.js are aieAudioPlayer, aieCompare and aieBoxes. The audio player fetches the file once and decodes it with the Web Audio API to get waveform peaks. It then plays the same blob through an object URL, which it revokes on detach. If the fetch or decode fails, the <audio> element loads the URL itself, and an error event or a failed play() switches the player to a note plus download. Starting one player pauses the others. The compare slider and the confidence control are native input[type=range] elements, so they work with the keyboard. Image preview uses a native <dialog> opened through data-aie-dialog-open. The dialog handler is not part of this diff.

The test module gets a styleguide_explorer plugin with sample SVG, WAV and PNG assets. Functional and kernel tests cover the new markup and theme hooks. A FunctionalJavascript test was also added, but its diff was not available to me.

item.title: #3586773: Generate AI API Explorer code examples with a shared builder that escapes input
item.description:

Summary

The AI API Explorer's "Code Example" output is now generated by a shared builder that exports user input as safe PHP literals. This replaces per-plugin HTML string concatenation, where quotes, $, backslashes or HTML in the input could produce broken or wrong PHP. The commit that shipped under this issue hardens the builder's edge cases: very large or small integers, floats, negative numbers after a minus sign, and user text inside comments. Copied examples therefore stay valid and reproduce the run.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Drupal\ai_api_explorer\CodeExample\CodeExample and PhpExporter build explorer code examples as plain PHP text, escaping every exported value.

Technical details

The shipped commit hardens the builder in modules/ai_api_explorer/src/CodeExample/. The builder itself was already in the repo, and I did not review the earlier commits that added it. CodeExample::line() takes a template where @0, @1 and so on are replaced by PhpExporter::export() output, so values are never pasted into quotes by hand. CodeExample::comment() turns line breaks into spaces and rewrites ?> as ? >, so run text cannot close the PHP tag and turn the rest of the example into HTML.

PhpExporter now prints PHP_INT_MIN as the constant, because its digits read back as a float. Floats are exported with serialize_precision temporarily set to -1 and then restored, so 0.1 + 0.2 keeps its exact value even on sites configured with precision 14. In line(), a negative exported value that directly follows a - is wrapped in parentheses (1-(-1)), which avoids producing the -- decrement operator.

The unit tests in CodeExampleTest cover these cases and check that output parses with CodeExample::parseError(). CodeExampleAssertionsTrait::codeFromElement() now fails when no pre code panel is found, instead of passing as an empty example.

item.title: #3586772: Store AI API Explorer runs per user in a new entity type, with a setting to turn it off
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +241/−13 · php +241/−13
  • Diff: b61ccef
  • Discussion: #3586772 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

The AI API Explorer can now keep a per-user history of runs (prompt, settings, output, errors, files) instead of forgetting everything on page reload. It is off by default, for new installs and for existing sites after the update, so nothing is stored until a site turns it on at /admin/config/ai/explorers/settings. With history on, a user sees only their own runs, and old runs are removed on cron by count and age limits. Anonymous visitors never get a stored history, even with it enabled. Administrators with the new permission can delete everyone's runs but cannot read or download them.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_api_explorer_update_16001() installs the ai_api_explorer_run entity type and default settings with history left off.
  • Config change: New ai_api_explorer.settings config with history.enabled (default off), history.max_runs (50) and history.max_age (30 days).
  • Permission change: New restricted administer ai api explorer permission: change history settings and delete other users' runs (not read them).
  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_run content entity type and ai_api_explorer.run_manager service (ExplorerRunManager) for storing, listing, purging and clearing explorer runs.

Technical details

Runs are stored in a new content entity ai_api_explorer_run (src/Entity/ExplorerRun.php, status enum ExplorerRunStatus). ExplorerRunAccessControlHandler allows view and update only to the authenticated owner who also has access ai prompt. administer ai api explorer adds delete on any run. Create access also requires an authenticated user, because every anonymous visitor is user 0.

ExplorerRunManager (ai_api_explorer.run_manager) is the entry point: create(), record(), getRuns(), getRecentFiles(), loadOwnRun(), clear(), saveFile(), purge(), enforceLimit(), deleteForUser(), deleteAll(). isEnabled() is true only for an authenticated user with history.enabled on. When it is false, record() keeps the run only in form state for that visit, and clear() leaves stored runs alone. purge() counts age from the changed timestamp, not created, so a run re-saved later, for example when one of its files is removed, is not purged early. Files are saved as managed files, in private:// when a private path is configured and otherwise in public:// (the settings form warns about this). hook_file_download() serves a run file only to its owner. Administrators are denied, including when history is off and no run references the file.

Output from explorers not yet moved to run history goes through ExplorerOutputFiles, which keeps unguessable file names. These files go to private://ai-explorers/ when a private path exists, otherwise to temporary://ai-explorers/. The settings form is ExplorerSettingsForm, with a confirmed "delete all runs" form (ExplorerRunsDeleteAllForm) and a local task on the explorers hub. Kernel tests cover limits, purge, anonymous users, Clear without history, file download access and the update hook.

Upgrade

Run database updates: ai_api_explorer_update_16001() installs the entity type and creates ai_api_explorer.settings with history off. To use the history, enable it at /admin/config/ai/explorers/settings and adjust the limits. To let other roles manage it, grant administer ai api explorer.

Summary

An AI API Explorer whose operation has no usable provider no longer answers "Access denied" to users who have the access ai prompt permission. The page now explains what to set up: it names the operation, says which installed providers can or cannot do it, and shows numbered setup steps with links. It can also point to another explorer as an alternative. If a provider throws an error while being checked, the page shows that error as a notice rather than breaking. Users without the permission still get 403.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: New ai-api-explorer-setup.html.twig template and template_preprocess_ai_api_explorer_setup() render the setup page; themes overriding explorer markup may want to style it.
  • New API: #[AiApiExplorer] attribute gains an operation_types array, and there is a new ai_api_explorer.availability service (ExplorerAvailability) plus an ai_api_explorer_setup theme hook.

Technical details

AiApiExplorerAccessChecker now returns AccessResult::allowedIf($plugin->hasAccess($account))->cachePerPermissions(). It no longer calls isActive(), so access depends only on the account. The decision moved into AiApiExplorerForm::buildForm(). It calls $plugin->isActive() inside a try/catch (\Throwable). If the explorer is inactive or a provider threw, it returns AiApiExplorerPluginBase::buildSetupNeeded($form, $error) instead of the normal form.

Plugins declare the operation types they call through the new operation_types argument of the #[AiApiExplorer] attribute. All bundled explorers were updated; ToolsExplorer declares chat. The setup page title and status are built from those operation types. An explorer that declares none, such as the Vector DB explorer, gets a "not available on this site" page with no provider steps, because what it lacks is not a provider. The base class has a getSetupAlternative() hook and addSetupAlternative() for pointing at another explorer.

A new service ai_api_explorer.availability (ExplorerAvailability) checks each provider separately with createInstance(), getSupportedOperationTypes() and isUsable(). It caches the result for the request. A provider that throws is recorded and logged to a new ai_api_explorer logger channel, so one broken provider does not hide the others. The AI API Explorer sub-module gets a shared look and feel: a "Set up" panel beside a "Results" panel that turns into two tabs on narrow screens, and reusable pieces such as run cards, status pills, score bars, code panels with copy, empty states, error cards, progress with cancel, dialogs and toasts. Colours follow Gin (including dark mode) and fall back to Claro-like colours. The same commit adds an optional per-user history of explorer runs, with a settings page at /admin/config/ai/explorers/settings. It also adds a "Create with AI" button for JSON schema fields, which is covered by the ai module's new use ai json schema generator permission. A follow-up commit fixes Cancel so the run button works again afterwards, rounds durations correctly and removes a Drupal 11.3 deprecation. The issue text says no explorer is migrated yet, so existing explorers should look and behave as before until their own issues land.

Impact

Affects module maintainers, front-end developers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_api_explorer_update_16001() installs the ai_api_explorer_run entity type. If ai_api_explorer.settings does not exist yet, it creates it with history enabled (50 runs, 30 days).
  • Config change: New ai_api_explorer.settings config with history.enabled, history.max_runs and history.max_age. The install default is enabled: false.
  • Permission change: New administer ai api explorer permission (restricted), needed for the explorer settings page and for deleting any user's stored runs. New use ai json schema generator permission in the ai module.
  • Theme change: Explorer forms render through new ai-api-explorer-* Twig templates and a container-query based explorer-ui.css. Colours follow Gin's custom properties, with Claro-like fallbacks.
  • New API: New ai_api_explorer_run content entity with ExplorerRunManager (ai_api_explorer.run_manager), the ExplorerUi helper, new theme hooks ai_api_explorer_form, _panel, _run, _code, _empty, _notice, and an ai_api_explorer/explorer_ui library.

Technical details

The layout is in css/explorer-ui.css and js/explorer-ui.js, attached through the new ai_api_explorer/explorer_ui library, with label_chips as a second library. The workspace uses CSS grid and responds to its own container width (container-type: inline-size, @container rules), not the viewport. Under 640px it becomes Set up and Results tabs with 44px touch targets. --aie-* custom properties map to --gin-* variables with fallbacks. With core Navigation, the sticky offset is reset to zero. Markup comes from ExplorerUi helpers and the theme hooks ai_api_explorer_form, _panel, _run, _code, _empty and _notice. Each hook has a template_preprocess_* function in the .module file. The plugin manager's createInstance() now passes the run manager, date formatter and time service to every AiApiExplorerPluginBase through setExplorerServices(). This avoids changing the create() signatures of explorers in other modules. A kernel test covers the theme hooks. The issue's task to replace getFormTemplate() with region helpers lives in AiApiExplorerPluginBase, which was among the files not returned by the diff tool, so it is not described here.

Run history is the ai_api_explorer_run content entity (ExplorerRunInterface). Its fields include explorer, status, provider, model, input, output, usage, error, duration, files and a source run. Access is limited to the owner, who also needs access ai prompt. administer ai api explorer additionally allows delete. hook_file_download() serves files under ai_api_explorer/ only to the run's owner or an administrator. Only images, audio, video, plain text, VTT, JSON, PDF and SubRip are served inline, and everything else is sent as an attachment. Cron, hook_user_predelete() and hook_user_cancel() handlers were added to Hook\AiApiExplorer. Their bodies were not in the diff returned by the tool.

Cancel in explorer-ui.js now runs the Ajax error clean-up, because an aborted jQuery request would otherwise leave Drupal's Ajax object "in progress" and ignore later presses. The running-timer interval is also cleared on detach. Each preprocess function is named as 'initial preprocess' in hook_theme(), because Drupal 11.3 deprecates finding template_preprocess_HOOK() by name. ExplorerUi::duration() now rounds before choosing the format, so 59.96 s reads 1 min 0 s and 9.999 s reads 10.0 s.

item.title: #3586777: Add "Create with AI" to the ai_json_schema form element
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +845/−37 · php +834/−37 · js +10 · txt +1
  • Diff: 532289d

Summary

The ai_json_schema form element can now show a "Create with AI" button. The user describes the answer they want, an LLM (the site's default chat model) writes a JSON schema, and the user reviews it as a field list or as JSON before clicking "Use this schema" to fill the element. The schema is adjusted to OpenAI-style strict mode rules, and the dialog lists what was changed. The button is opt-in per element, so existing uses are unchanged. Using it requires the new use ai json schema generator permission. The shipped commit also hardens the generator: values in the review dialog are escaped once, empty objects are no longer written as [], more schema constructs are handled, and model errors are logged.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: New use ai json schema generator permission gates the Create with AI dialog.
  • API change: JsonSchemaGeneratorInterface gains encode(); messages and type labels from normalize(), validate() and describeFields() are now safe HTML.
  • New API: #ai_generate and #ai_generate_answer on the ai_json_schema element; JsonSchemaGeneratorInterface::encode().

Technical details

The feature is split across the ai module's AiJsonSchema element (#ai_generate, #ai_generate_answer), the ai.json_schema_generate route (/admin/config/ai/json-schema/generate, AiJsonSchemaGenerateForm) and the ai.json_schema_generator service. The shipped commit (532289d5) is the hardening pass on those pieces. The base feature came in with the earlier commit 00a5a57ec, which also built the AI API Explorers layout.

In JsonSchemaGenerator, normalize() now also covers these cases:

  • It applies strict rules inside anyOf, oneOf, $defs and definitions.
  • It turns const into a one-item enum.
  • It infers a missing type from properties or items.
  • It gives an object with no fields an empty properties map and additionalProperties: false.
  • It rewrites oneOf as anyOf only when the alternatives' types cannot overlap (cannotOverlap()). Otherwise validate() reports oneOf as unsupported.

nullable() adds null to every keyword that restricts values (type, enum, anyOf/oneOf) instead of always inventing a type. A $ref is wrapped as anyOf: [$ref, {type: null}]. describeFields() uses acceptsNull() to decide Required versus Can be empty. validate() also reports required names that don't exist in properties.

JsonSchemaGeneratorInterface gains encode(array $schema): string. It casts properties, $defs and definitions to objects so an empty map or one with numeric names is not written as a JSON list, which strict structured output rejects. The form's JSON view and useCallback() now use it. Messages from normalize(), validate() and the type label in describeFields() are now documented as safe HTML (values escaped once), and the form renders them as #markup. The form's error path also calls Error::logException() on the ai logger channel.

Upgrade

To opt an element in:

'#type' => 'ai_json_schema',
'#ai_generate' => TRUE,
'#ai_generate_answer' => $last_answer,

Grant use ai json schema generator to roles that should see the button. Custom classes implementing JsonSchemaGeneratorInterface must add encode(array $schema): string. Code that consumes the normalize() and validate() messages, or the describeFields() type labels, should render them as markup, not as plain text.

item.title: #3586821: Cache flush on VDB installation does not work
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +2/−0 · yml +2
  • Diff: 33ff73a
  • Discussion: #3586821 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Installing a module that alters Vector DB provider definitions now takes effect immediately. Before, the cached VDB provider plugin definitions were not cleared on module install, so the alter was missing until a manual cache rebuild. Config installed by that module could therefore run against the unaltered plugin class.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The ai.vdb_provider plugin manager is not named plugin.manager.*, so core's PluginManagerPass never tagged it plugin_manager_cache_clear. ai_modules_installed() clears ai_provider_plugins but not ai_vdb_provider_info_plugins. The commit adds tags: [{ name: plugin_manager_cache_clear }] to ai.vdb_provider in ai.services.yml. This clears the definitions cache before config install, which a hook_modules_installed() implementation cannot do. The issue also notes that a 1.x backport of #3535939 would help, but that is not part of this commit.

Upgrade

No action needed. Rebuild caches once after updating so the container picks up the new service tag.

item.title: #3586819: ChatFormBlock::blockAccess() passes NULL to load() when no AI Assistant is configured (array_flip() warning)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +10/−1 · php +10/−1
  • Diff: 2d95e74
  • Discussion: #3586819 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

An AI Chatbot block with no AI Assistant selected no longer triggers an array_flip() PHP warning in the log. This showed up on sites where a page builder or similar tool creates every block plugin with default configuration and checks access on each one. The unconfigured block is now simply treated as not accessible.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ChatFormBlock::blockAccess() passed $this->configuration['ai_assistant'] straight to the ai_assistant entity storage load(). With default configuration that value is empty, so EntityStorageBase::loadMultiple() received [NULL] and logged the warning. blockAccess() now reads the ID first and returns AccessResult::forbidden('No AI Assistant configured.') when it is not a non-empty string. Otherwise it loads the entity and runs the existing exists and enabled checks. This matches the guard already in ChatFormBlock::build() and the unconfigured handling in DeepChatFormBlock::blockAccess() (#3577813).
